tier_justification: Known informally (C11 6.5p6-7; the type-based alias analysis of compilers) and, at the level of single memory operations on statically typed memory trees, mechanized by Krebbers (CPP 2013, Coq lemma mem_non_aliasing). That lemma is symmetric because CH2O objects receive their type at allocation; it is not a statement about reordering program instructions. R1 is a contextual-refinement statement for the load-hoisting transformation in a model where stores re-type allocated storage, in which the symmetric reading fails (R1b, R1c). No mechanized statement of this form was found in the sources examined.
plain_claim: Under the effective-type semantics with the standard discipline (character exemption), if T is not u8, U is not u8, T and U share no leaf scalar type (NoCommonLeaf T U), and the load's destination register differs from the store's source register, then moving a load at type T above an earlier store at type U is a refinement in every context, from every initial state, and for every address pair.

hypotheses.name: hT : T ≠ Ty.u8
hypotheses.purpose: A byte load may read bytes of any effective type (the character exemption), so after the store it is defined and sees the new byte.
hypotheses.witness_class: overlapping addresses p = q = 0 on untyped allocated storage (freshAt 0 16), T = u8, U = u32

hypotheses.name: hU : U ≠ Ty.u8
hypotheses.purpose: After a byte store, a later typed load of the same bytes can still be defined and then sees the new byte. In the toy a byte store into allocated storage keeps the byte's tag (a modeling choice: in the literal text of C11 6.5p6 a character-type store modifies the stored value, which ends the period in which a previously stored effective type applies, and later accesses then take the type of their own lvalue). The counterexamples do not depend on that choice: one uses fresh storage with no tag, the other a declared u32 object, whose type no store changes.
hypotheses.witness_class: overlapping addresses p = q = 0, T = u32, U = u8: on untyped allocated storage with no tag (hoist_E_needs_store_ne_u8), and on a declared u32 object, where the witness state satisfies DeclaredOn on the load's range and the hoist is not sound even from the states declared on that range (hoist_E_needs_store_ne_u8_on_declared)

hypotheses.name: hTU : NoCommonLeaf T U
hypotheses.purpose: Types sharing a leaf can alias: a struct load can read a member just stored. 'T ≠ U' is not enough (pair vs u32).
hypotheses.witness_class: overlapping addresses p = q = 0 on untyped allocated storage, T = pair, U = u32

hypotheses.name: hsr : s ≠ r
hypotheses.purpose: Register data dependence: if the load overwrites the store's source register, the store writes a different value.
hypotheses.witness_class: disjoint addresses p = 8, q = 0 on untyped allocated storage, s = r = 0, T = f32, U = u32

nonvacuity_witness: Scalar instance T = f32, U = u32, p = 8, q = 0, s = 1, r = 0 (hoist_E_nonvacuous) and struct instance T = pair, U = u16, p = 0, q = 8, s = 1, r = 0 (hoist_E_nonvacuous_struct): all hypotheses hold, the source block (with suffix out 1) is defined from a concrete state, and the target gives the same outcome.
non_claims: The statement covers the hoist direction (a load moved earlier, above a store). Its hypotheses do not license the sink (a load moved later, below a store) or the swap of two stores: R1b and R1c are instances (T = u32, U = f32, the same address, untyped allocated storage) that satisfy the type hypotheses and in which those replacements are not refinements.

Does not say that T ≠ U suffices: a struct and its member type are distinct but alias (hoist_E_needs_noCommonLeaf). NoCommonLeaf is a per-byte criterion: it is coarser than C's 'neither type is (an aggregate containing) the other' whenever two distinct struct types share a scalar member type (they share a leaf, so the result does not apply to them, although C11, CH2O and LLVM struct-path TBAA can treat them as non-aliasing), and it ignores offsets, so it cannot separate two fields of the same scalar type at different offsets. Per-byte tags carry no object boundaries: a pair load of bytes written by a separate u32 store and f32 store is defined in this model (Toy.Tbaa.Examples.stepE_pair_load_from_member_stores_defined). C's compatible-type relation, unions, qualifiers and signedness variants are not modeled.

The refinement is from the effective-type semantics to itself. It does not say the transformation is sound for an implementation that gives programs untyped-memory semantics (for example a C compiler run in a no-strict-aliasing mode): under untyped memory the hoist across a same-address store is not a refinement (R2). Running the transformed effective-type program on untyped memory is covered by composing with R4b, which is not stated as a separate theorem.
Does not cover memcpy-based or byte-based reordering, nor reordering across unknown code. Across a call that may free, reallocate or memcpy-re-type the storage, nothing is claimed (not modeled).

Toy model: straight-line programs with constant addresses; five access types (u8, u16, u32, f32, and a padding-free struct pair = {u32, f32}); every byte list of the right length is valid for every type (no uninitialized bytes, pointer provenance or alignment); no unions, qualifiers, signed/unsigned variants, arrays, pointers stored in memory, allocation or deallocation, object lifetimes, control flow, calls, or concurrency. The observable behaviour of a run is its output trace together with whether it terminates normally or with undefined behaviour, and undefined behaviour does not retract output already emitted.
These are statements about the toy model; they neither establish nor refute the corresponding claims about C, C++, LLVM or Rust.

tier_justification: That untyped memory gives no type-based alias facts is folklore (the Rust Reference states its aliasing undefined behaviour in terms of references and Box; LLVM IR memory has no types); made precise here with an explicit witness and a universally quantified refutation.
plain_claim: Under the untyped semantics, for all types T and U (with no condition relating them) and every address p: (1) from the witness state uWit U p, the target [load 1 T p, store U p 0, out 1] has the behaviour 'print T.size zero bytes', which the source [store U p 0, load 1 T p, out 1] lacks; and (2) for all registers s and r, hoisting a T-load from p above a U-store to the same address p is not a refinement. Consequently, for every criterion C on pairs of access types: if, whenever C T U holds, this same-address hoist is a refinement under the untyped semantics for every address p and every pair of distinct registers s ≠ r, then C holds for no pair of types (no_type_criterion_licenses_same_addr_hoist_U); and if, whenever C T U holds, the same-address hoist is a refinement under the untyped semantics for at least one address p and one pair of registers s, r, then C holds for no pair of types (no_type_criterion_licenses_same_addr_hoist_U_at_one_site).
nonvacuity_witness: T = f32, U = u32, p = 0 (fully proved instance of part (1), hoist_unsound_U_instance). The premises of both corollaries are satisfied by the empty criterion C := fun _ _ => False (no_type_criterion_premises_satisfiable); by the corollaries, every criterion satisfying them holds for no pair of types.

plain_claim: Under the effective-type semantics with the standard discipline, for every state σ, type T, source p, destination q (overlapping ranges allowed) and register s: memcpy q p T.size followed by a T-load from q and out s terminates normally, printing exactly the bytes that were at p, if and only if MemcpyLoadOk σ T p q holds (both ranges allocated, and at each byte offset i the leaf T.leafAt i is compatible with the destination byte's declared leaf if that byte belongs to a declared object, and with the source byte's tag otherwise). Corollary: if a T-load from p would pass the checks (ReadableAt) and the destination range is allocated and its declared bytes accept T (ReceivesAt), the copy-then-load is defined and returns the bytes at p.
nonvacuity_witness: Both sides of the characterization are inhabited: copying the u32 object of objSt u32 into untyped storage, and memcpy punning of an f32 object into a declared u32 object, satisfy MemcpyLoadOk and run to completion; copying an f32 object into allocated storage and loading it at u32 violates MemcpyLoadOk and is undefined (memcpy_then_load_nonvacuous). The corollary's hypotheses hold for objSt u32 (memcpy_corollary_nonvacuous).

non_claims: Does not say that memcpy avoids effective-type undefined behaviour in general. Under (E), as in C11 6.5p6, memcpy into allocated storage (no declared type) copies the source's effective type, so loading the copy at an incompatible type is undefined (memcpy_then_load_nonvacuous, last two conjuncts); by the characterization (memcpy_then_typed_load_defined_E_iff) and the definition of MemcpyLoadOk, if the copy-then-load terminates normally printing the bytes that were at p, then at every byte offset where the source byte's tag is incompatible with T's leaf, the destination byte belongs to a declared object whose leaf is compatible with T's leaf (memcpy punning at an incompatible type goes through declared destination bytes); an instance of memcpy punning into a declared object is Toy.Tbaa.Examples.stepE_memcpy_into_declared_defined. In C++ (N4950 [cstring.syn] p3, [intro.object] p10) memcpy implicitly creates objects in the destination, so the corresponding C++ program with malloc'd storage can be defined; C++ is not modeled.
The corollary's ReadableAt is not necessary: memcpy punning into a declared object is defined although the source is not readable at the destination's type (readable_source_not_necessary).

Defined typed use of the copy relies on memcpy transferring tags, not on the character exemption alone: a loop of u8 loads and u8 stores through a register leaves an f32-typed destination f32-typed, so a u32 load of it is undefined (Toy.Tbaa.Examples.byte_loop_copy_does_not_transfer_effective_type). C11 6.5p6 also transfers the effective type for copies 'as an array of character type'; the toy does not model that clause for explicit byte loops.
Says nothing about copies whose length differs from T.size or that start at another offset.

The toy's memcpy reads every source byte before writing any destination byte, which is the semantics of C's memmove, and its step has no condition on overlap; copies between overlapping ranges can be defined in the toy, and the plain claim's 'overlapping ranges allowed' refers to this primitive (memcpy_overlap_defined_examples: copying [0, 4) to [2, 6) prints the original source bytes, and a self-copy is defined). ISO C11 (N1570 7.24.2.1p2) makes memcpy between overlapping objects undefined behaviour; that undefinedness is not modeled, so for overlapping ranges the statement describes a memmove-like copy, not C's memcpy.

Toy model: straight-line programs with constant addresses; five access types (u8, u16, u32, f32, and a padding-free struct pair = {u32, f32}); every byte list of the right length is valid for every type (no uninitialized bytes, pointer provenance or alignment); no unions, qualifiers, signed/unsigned variants, arrays, pointers stored in memory, allocation or deallocation, object lifetimes, control flow, calls, or concurrency. tier_justification: Folklore (effective types add undefined behaviour and remove no untyped behaviour); made precise here as a refinement for every configuration, program and state, together with the exact condition under which the converse inclusion fails.
plain_claim: For every configuration cfg, program P and initial state σ, every behaviour of the untyped execution of P from erase σ is a behaviour of the effective-type execution of P from σ under cfg. Moreover (behE_not_refines_behU_iff), for every cfg, P and σ, the converse inclusion (every behaviour of the effective-type execution is a behaviour of the untyped execution) fails if and only if the effective-type execution stops at a type fault (TypeFaults cfg P σ) and, in addition, the untyped execution from erase σ either terminates normally (UDefined P (erase σ)) or has a strictly longer output trace than the effective-type execution.
nonvacuity_witness: No hypotheses. An instance where the inclusion is strict is behU_refines_behE_strict_instance; both sides of the converse characterization occur: behE_not_refines_behU_of_uDefined_nonvacuous (a type-faulting program with a defined untyped run, where the converse fails, and a byte-reading program, where it holds), behE_not_refines_behU_without_uDefined (the converse fails through the trace-length disjunct) and behE_refines_behU_masked_instance (a type-faulting program for which the converse holds).

Declared objects in the toy have no lifetime end. Storage that is reused for a different type (C++ placement new or the end of an object's lifetime; stack slots reused across non-overlapping variable lifetimes, such as { int x; } { float y; } or llvm.lifetime.start/end) is not declared storage in this sense, and nothing is claimed for it.

NoCommonLeaf is a per-byte criterion: it is coarser than C's 'neither type is (an aggregate containing) the other' whenever two distinct struct types share a scalar member type (they share a leaf, so the result does not apply to them, although C11, CH2O and LLVM struct-path TBAA can treat them as non-aliasing), and it ignores offsets, so it cannot separate two fields of the same scalar type at different offsets. C's compatible-type relation, unions, qualifiers and signedness variants are not modeled.

The tightness witness for DeclaredOn is an overlapping address pair (p = q = 0 on allocated storage).

Declared objects in the toy have no lifetime end. Storage that is reused for a different type (C++ placement new or the end of an object's lifetime; stack slots reused across non-overlapping variable lifetimes, such as { int x; } { float y; } or llvm.lifetime.start/end) is not declared storage in this sense, and nothing is claimed for it.

NoCommonLeaf is a per-byte criterion: it is coarser than C's 'neither type is (an aggregate containing) the other' whenever two distinct struct types share a scalar member type (they share a leaf, so the result does not apply to them, although C11, CH2O and LLVM struct-path TBAA can treat them as non-aliasing), and it ignores offsets, so it cannot separate two fields of the same scalar type at different offsets. Per-byte tags carry no object boundaries: a pair load of bytes written by a separate u32 store and f32 store is defined in this model (Toy.Tbaa.Examples.stepE_pair_load_from_member_stores_defined). C's compatible-type relation, unions, qualifiers and signedness variants are not modeled.

Toy model: straight-line programs with constant addresses; five access types (u8, u16, u32, f32, and a padding-free struct pair = {u32, f32}); every byte list of the right length is valid for every type (no uninitialized bytes, pointer provenance or alignment); no unions, qualifiers, signed/unsigned variants, arrays, pointers stored in memory, allocation or deallocation, object lifetimes, control flow, calls, or concurrency. The observable behaviour of a run is its output trace together with whether it terminates normally or with undefined behaviour, and undefined behaviour does not retract output already emitted.
These are statements about the toy model; they neither establish nor refute the corresponding claims about C, C++, LLVM or Rust.
